summary: Describes the APEX presence service, found at the well-known endpoint named apex=presence. It manages presence information for APEX endpoints, meaning whether and how they can be reached. The protocol is historic.

eli5.summary: A chat program shows whether your friend is online. The APEX presence service did that job for APEX programs. It is now historic.

questions: what is the apex presence service
how do subscriptions work in apex presence
subtitle: How APEX endpoints share whether they are reachable

tldr.problem: Applications need a way to share and query whether they are online or available, along with multiple ways they can be reached.
tldr.mechanism: The APEX presence service runs at a well-known endpoint and accepts operations to update, subscribe to, or watch presence information for any endpoint in a domain.
tldr.outcome: Applications can request presence updates when status changes, learn who is watching their presence, and manage complex reachability information, but the system was experimental and is now historic.

today: RFC 3343 is Historic; it was an Experimental protocol and is no longer under development. The APEX presence service system did not see widespread adoption and is superseded by other approaches to presence management.

sections.title: What the Presence Service Does
sections.content:
RFC 3343 defines the APEX presence service, which runs on a well-known endpoint named apex=presence within an administrative domain. The service lets applications share information about whether they are reachable and how they can be contacted.

The presence service sits on top of the APEX core, a best-effort datagram network. Applications communicate with the service by sending data to the well-known endpoint; for example, applications in example.com use apex=presence@example.com. The service tracks presence entries for each endpoint in the domain, containing all the ways that endpoint can be reached and whether each is currently available.
sections.eli5: The presence service is like a lobby phone that knows who is in the building and how to reach them. Applications call the lobby to ask about someone or to update their own status.

sections.title: Core Operations
sections.content:
The presence service supports six main operations, each carried in XML elements. A publish operation tells the service to update an endpoint's presence information, including how it can be reached and until when. A subscribe operation asks for an endpoint's current presence and then sends updates whenever the presence changes, for a time set by the subscriber. A watch operation lets an endpoint learn who is subscribing to its own presence, again with periodic updates.

When an endpoint no longer needs updates, a terminate operation cancels the subscription or watch. The service replies to operations with a reply element, and it sends a notify element to watchers whenever a subscription starts or stops. Each operation carries a transaction ID so the service can match replies to requests.
sections.eli5: Publish is updating your status. Subscribe is asking for someone's status changes. Watch is watching who is asking about you. Terminate stops the updates. The service always replies with a yes or error.

sections.title: Presence Entries and Tuples
sections.content:
Each endpoint has one presence entry, which holds a publisher attribute (the endpoint's name), a lastUpdate timestamp, optional publisherInfo (a URL with arbitrary information), and one or more tuple elements. Each tuple describes one way an endpoint can be reached: a destination URI (such as apex:fred/appl=im@example.com or mailto:fred@flintstone.com), an availableUntil timestamp showing when that destination will stop accepting messages, optional tupleInfo (arbitrary data about that destination), and zero or more capability elements that describe what kinds of content that destination can receive.

To update a presence entry, an application must include the current lastUpdate value to ensure only one update succeeds at a time (an atomic update mechanism). The service rejects updates with a stale timestamp.
sections.eli5: A presence entry lists all the ways to reach one person. Each way is a tuple: an address, a deadline, and what kinds of messages it accepts.

sections.title: Access Control and Service Rules
sections.content:
The service enforces access control by checking tokens stored in the APEX access service. Three tokens control what an application can do: presence:subscribe allows reading another endpoint's presence, presence:watch allows watching who is subscribed to you, and presence:publish allows updating your own presence. The service also validates that the target is in the same administrative domain and that the endpoint exists.

A subscribe operation with zero duration performs a one-time poll of the presence information without setting up ongoing updates. The service sends a terminate operation when a subscription or watch reaches its duration limit. Either party can cancel early by sending a terminate operation, but updates sent before the cancellation arrives may still be in transit.
sections.eli5: The service checks that you have permission to read, watch, or update presence. It also makes sure the endpoint is in your domain. You can ask for a one-time snapshot or continuous updates for a time limit.

sections.title: Security and Timestamps
sections.content:
The RFC notes that timestamps issued by the presence service may disclose location information if services use precise timezone information. Applications concerned about privacy can use the special timezone value -00:00 after converting local time accordingly, which obscures location.

The service must maintain information about both presence entries and in-progress operations in persistent storage to ensure consistency and recovery from failures.
sections.eli5: If you use exact timezone information, someone could figure out where you are. You can hide it with a special timezone code if you want privacy.
